title: FluxCD and how it compares with ArgoCD

videos.script: Flux does the same job as Argo CD, and it is built the other way round. {{same}} Instead of one central object, it has a chain of small ones. One fetches the repository. Another applies a path of it. Each has a controller of its own. {{chain}} First, Argo CD leaves. Two agents on the same objects would fight, so you retire it, and take away its access to the repository the same day. {{retire}} Then you bootstrap Flux. The usual command pushes to main, and main is protected. So you do its three steps by hand, and the commit goes through review like any other. {{bootstrap}} You will see Flux reconcile on a timer rather than on events. You will pause it on the record, and make a push reach the cluster in seconds with a webhook. {{webhook}} Last, the two tools side by side, and why the rest of the course uses Flux. {{compare}}
